title: Does the hanger-fit width rule hold on fabrics with published KES-FB bending rigidity and weight?
lede: does "arm 1 cm wider than the half shoulder" hold on four fabrics with published KES-FB bending rigidity (0.0066–0.125) and weight (12.5–24.6 mg/cm²)? Best offset is +1 cm in all 12 cases (with stretch swept 40–800 N/m); heavy suiting at 40 N/m nearly ties with +2 cm. B and weight sourced; stretch swept; tee geometry assumed.
summary: hanger-sweep could not find measured fabric constants and swept them. This run uses a published KES-FB table (Ramaiah et al., fibre2fashion PDF, Table 3) for four fabrics: cotton single jersey, elastane single jersey, cotton shirting and heavy cotton suiting (bending rigidity 0.0066–0.125 gf·cm<sup>2</sup>/cm, weight 12.5–24.6 mg/cm<sup>2</sup>). On an M tee shape the best arm half width of the stock hanger is the half shoulder + 1 cm in all 12 cases (4 fabrics × stretch stiffness 40, 150, 800 N/m), best error 0.18–0.83 cm RMS; the suiting at 40 N/m nearly ties with +2 cm (0.83 vs 0.87). Bending rigidity and weight are sourced; stretch stiffness is swept because the table lacks it; the garment geometry and the tee mass scale are hanger-fit's assumptions for every fabric; the source fabrics are unfinished.
